item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-21
item.description: One number settles this morning. On 2026-11-20, at the OpenAtom Developer Conference in Zhengzhou, Loongson and the OpenAtom Foundation established the LoongArch Community — the country's first comprehensive open-source community around a self-developed instruction set, with 22 founding member organisations across chips, operating systems, complete machines and research institutes, and OpenLA132, a LoongArch open processor core, already online. The repository behind OpenLA132, github.com/loongson/OpenLACores, was created on 2026-10-08, carries the Mulan PSL v2 licence the Foundation publishes, is forty-three days old, and holds six commits from four authors, of which exactly one came from outside its corporate lineage. That is the measurement no charter answers: not who governs the community, but what the community has so far produced. Two of the day's other documents are the same measurement arriving from other directions — the statutory annual filings of the Foundation, which show CNY 223.6 million of donations over 2020–23 with zero yuan of foreign donations in any year and CNY 20.7 million of government subsidy arriving in 2023 after none in 2022, and a semi-official WeChat account calmly explaining that the certification most often read as a procurement monopoly is a three-year licence that has to be re-earned from scratch, because the kernel version is a mandatory field in the notice. One city is buying a layer. One foundation is opening a door in its core. Both are being audited by their own bookkeeping, and the audit is not unkind — it is merely exact.
